scenes.line1: How fast is your code, really?
scenes.say: How fast is your code, really? What does Big-O actually measure?

scenes.label: Big-O
scenes.sub: Describes how time or space grows as input increases.
scenes.say: Big-O describes how an algorithm's time or space grows as input size increases.
Always state both time and space complexity. For example, O of n time and O of one space.

scenes.title: Python List Append
scenes.say: Appending to a Python list is usually constant time, but resizing bumps it up to linear time. On average, it's O of one—amortized.

scenes.question: What if you skip worst-case analysis?
scenes.right: Interviewers expect you to mention worst, average, or amortized cases.
scenes.say: Don't skip worst-case, average, or amortized cases. Interviewers expect you to mention them.
